extra.message: UsersHandler.post reads uname and pwd from the POST body and concatenates them directly into a SQL statement: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM Users WHERE User ='" + uname + "' AND Password ='" + pwd + "'"). No parameterization or escaping is used, so an attacker can inject SQL (e.g. username admin' -- or ' OR '1'='1) to bypass authentication and read arbitrary rows from the Users table.

ServerHandler.post takes the user-controlled 'server' argument and concatenates it into a shell command executed via os.popen('ping -c 3 ' + server). Because the string is passed to a shell without sanitization, an attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands using shell metacharacters (e.g. server=127.0.0.1; id; cat /etc/passwd) and achieve remote command execution.

StaticHandler.get receives the URL-captured path via the /static/(.*) route and joins it into a filesystem path ('static/' + path) that is opened with open(static_file, 'r'). No normalization or containment check is performed, so a request such as /static/../../../../etc/passwd escapes the static directory and reads arbitrary files from the server.

ContentHandler.get takes the user-controlled 'file' query parameter and concatenates it directly into the path 'read/' + file_name before calling io.open(). No sanitization is applied, so a request such as /read?file=../../../../etc/passwd traverses outside the intended read/ directory and discloses arbitrary files.

SearchHandler.get passes the raw 'q' parameter as both 'query' and 'link' to search.html, and the template renders them with the {% raw %} tag (lines 70-71), which disables Tornado's automatic HTML escaping. An attacker can craft /search?q=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> to execute arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser (reflected XSS). The handler additionally sets X-XSS-Protection: 0, removing the browser's built-in filter.

SearchHandler.get explicitly sets the response header 'X-XSS-Protection' to '0', disabling the browser's reflected-XSS filtering. This security misconfiguration makes the reflected XSS in search.html reliably exploitable in browsers that honor the header.

The Tornado application settings enable debug mode ('debug': True). In debug mode Tornado returns full stack traces and detailed error pages to clients, exposing source paths, internal logic and library versions. Debug mode should never be enabled in a production deployment.

create_db() embeds plaintext account credentials directly in source code (admin/admin, test-user/test@123, sagar/lall0l, alias/ohrealli, jacky/st40ngp@55, sam/tomTOM123, maxi/D@ni3lDizaark, lelol/Leeee@Looo@$). These credentials are committed to version control and can be used directly to authenticate.

UploadHandler.post trusts the client-supplied filename: it derives the file extension from original_fname via os.path.splitext and writes the uploaded body to /tmp/<random><extension> with no validation of content type or extension. An attacker can upload files of any type (e.g. .py, .html, .sh), enabling arbitrary content storage and potential code execution if the upload directory is later served or processed.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: The Application settings dict does not enable xsrf_cookies, so Tornado performs no CSRF token validation. All state-changing POST handlers (UploadHandler.post, UsersHandler.post, ServerHandler.post) accept requests without an anti-CSRF token, allowing an attacker to submit forged requests on behalf of a victim (e.g. to trigger the command-injection endpoint or upload files).

ServerHandler.post, which executes OS commands derived from user input, has no authentication or authorization check (no @tornado.web.authenticated decorator, no get_current_user() or prepare() check, and no auth configured on the Application). Any unauthenticated remote user can invoke this sensitive functionality. The same absence of access control applies to UploadHandler.post and ContentHandler.get.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
